title: Zangarmarsh
body: Zangarmarsh is a vast wetland in western Outland, where mushrooms taller than any tree rise over still pools and glowing fungi light the gloom. Sporebats drift overhead, and the giants that wade through the bogs are themselves made of living fungus. When the druids of the Cenarion Expedition arrived, they expected to find only small pockets of life and instead found a thriving wilderness. Then they noticed that the water was falling, and the marsh has begun to wither. Many peoples share the land: the draenei of Telredor and the Kurenai of the Orebor Harborage, the Darkspear trolls of Zabra'jin and Swamprat Post, the peaceful sporelings of Sporeggar, savage tribes of Lost Ones, the Ango'rosh ogres, who are cutting down the mushroom forests of the north, and the naga, who hold the shores of the great lakes, keep a stronghold beneath Serpent Lake in Coilfang Reservoir and have attacked the druids since the day they arrived.

title: Cenarion Refuge
body: The Cenarion Refuge stands in the east of the marsh, at the end of the road from Hellfire Peninsula, and is the headquarters of the Cenarion Expedition. Its leader, Ysiel Windsinger, keeps watch from a balcony behind the inn, while Warden Hamoot and his wardens guard against the naga, who have attacked the druids since the day they arrived. Two great ancients, Ashyen, an Ancient of Lore, and Keleth, an Ancient of War, stand among the buildings and bless those the Expedition trusts. Lauranna Thar'well catalogues the marsh's plants, the Broken refugee Ikeyen teaches the druids what he knows of the land, and Morthis Whisperwing waits for a worthy apprentice while his two birds, Rook and Corvax, circle overhead.

title: Umbrafen Lake and Darkcrest Shore
body: Umbrafen Lake lies southwest of the Cenarion Refuge. On Darkcrest Shore the naga work a great steam pump, guarded by Darkcrest slavers and sorceresses who drive Dreghood Broken as drudges, and the pump's overseer threatens intruders with the wrath of Warlord Kalithresh. The lake itself is home to Umbrafen eels, whose meat is a staple of the draenei at Telredor, and to mire hydras, whose thick scales resist the damp of the marsh.

parts.body: It was here that the Cenarion Expedition first went looking for the cause of the falling water, and here that it found its first answer. The pump on Darkcrest Shore is drawing the lake away, and with that discovery the naga's attacks on the druids at last made sense.

title: Umbrafen Village
body: South of the Cenarion Refuge lies Umbrafen Village, home of the Umbrafen, a tribe of Lost Ones who took the side of the naga. The Broken who escaped them call the Umbrafen the worst of all the traitor tribes: their oracles, seers and witchdoctors use dark magic to trap and enslave others, and they are especially cruel to slaves who flee. Their leader is Kataru. Those taken here are not easily freed. The druid Kayra Longmane was seized by a band of them while gathering herbs nearby, and Ikeyen of the Refuge still fears that they will come for him.

title: Funggor Cavern
body: Funggor Cavern opens in the far south of the marsh, near the border with Nagrand and south of Umbrafen Village. It is the home of the sporeloks, who have lately been overrun by marsh dredgers and marsh lurkers that have invaded their caves. The Expedition sent watchers to study the cavern, but had to recall them after repeated attacks by the marsh beasts, and Warden Hamoot believes that killing their leader, Lord Klaq, would put an end to it. The Broken Ikeyen hid here after escaping the Umbrafen, only to flee again when the beasts and spore men fought over the cave, leaving behind everything he owned.

title: Telredor
body: Telredor is built atop a giant mushroom in the east of the marsh, its halls lit by cultivated fulgor spores, since little in the swamp will burn. For centuries it was a secluded retreat for draenei priests and pilgrims who seldom saw visitors. When the orcs began attacking the draenei, refugees arrived in growing numbers, and Anchorite Ahuurn and the other priests turned the shrine into a haven to which many owe their lives. Today it is the Alliance's stronghold in the marsh. Vindicator Idaar watches over the land, Noraani and Haalrun, once its only outsiders, help feed the newcomers, and a dwarf of the Explorers' League has come to settle a score with a giant wasp.

title: The Dead Mire
body: The Dead Mire, northeast of Telredor, is a stretch of cracked and parched ground where the marsh has dried away, and almost everything living on it withers. Withered giants stalk it, attacking anything in their path, while parched hydras and withered bog lords roam the baked mud. Threshalisks lie in the dirt playing dead before they charge, and pieces of steam pumps lie scattered about. No one who has ventured in has ever reported seeing anything alive and well there.

parts.body: A troll scout from Swamprat Post, Jyoba, came here to explore and never returned. His body lies in the mire beside a spilled inkwell, his weapon still sheathed, and flecks of withered fungus on it suggest that one of the withered giants caught him by surprise as he sat writing his report.

title: Swamprat Post
body: Swamprat Post is the Horde's newest outpost in the marsh, raised by Darkspear trolls just south of the Dead Mire. Shadow Hunter Denjai sent Zurai there with a small band of builders and warriors to give the Horde a presence on the eastern border, after the Alliance began fortifying old draenei ruins, and to tighten the Horde's hold on the roads in and out of the marsh. Marshfang rippers are everywhere, mail armor soon fails in the damp, and the cook answers every complaint of hunger by handing over an axe and pointing at a mushroom. Meanwhile Reavij pines for Magasha, Magasha has eyes only for Zurai, and the witch doctor's charms have done nothing to change that.

title: Feralfen Village
body: Feralfen Village lies in the south central marsh, home of the Feralfen, said to be the most powerful tribe of Lost Ones in Zangarmarsh and keepers of potent medicine. Their mystics, hunters and druids have turned to the worship of animal spirits, and they carve idols and totems in honor of the spirits they revere. Just north of the village roams Blacksting, a giant bog wasp that drove off the first Explorers' League party to camp there.

parts.body: The tribe's carvings honor two spirits, a serpent and a bird. Seer Janidi of Zabra'jin, who studied the captured totems, scorns the bird as weak and capricious, but judges that the serpent wields considerable power.

parts.body: The idols show a fixation on birds, which is a puzzle, since no birds are native to Zangarmarsh. Anchorite Ahuurn of Telredor wonders whether the tribe once met the arakkoa, who to a shamanistic people might seem the very embodiment of a powerful bird spirit.

title: Boha'mu Ruins
body: The Boha'mu Ruins are the remains of a draenei temple southwest of Telredor, one of several shrines once kept by a small order of anchorites and vindicators. Contact with its keepers was lost during the orcs' war on the draenei, and the Feralfen Lost Ones have since made the ruins their own. Their elder, Kuruti, dwells in the temple itself, and the tribe's mystics and hunters walk its old stones.

parts.body: To the draenei of Telredor the Feralfen's choice of home is a sign. They must remember something of their heritage and of what this place once meant, and Anchorite Ahuurn hopes the temple may hold the key to redeeming the Lost Ones and reuniting the many threads of the draenei.

title: The Lagoon and Darkcrest Enclave
body: The Lagoon lies in the south central marsh, a broad stretch of water haunted by lagoon eels, mire hydras and lagoon walkers, among them a great one called Marsh Baron Brok. On its shore stands the Darkcrest Enclave, where the naga run another of their steam pumps. Darkcrest taskmasters and sirens keep Dreghood Broken at the work, and the enclave answers to Rajah Haghazed, leader of the Darkcrest naga. The Cenarion Expedition has tied the Darkcrest to many attacks on its people, and a bounty posted at the Refuge warns that the rajah is extremely dangerous.

title: Cenarion Watchpost
body: The Cenarion Watchpost is a small camp in the southwest of the marsh, west of Quagg Ridge, where Watcher Leesa'oh studies the sporelings and bog lords. She believes that all things in nature are bound in one web, and that anyone who interferes without understanding it will surely cause destruction, so she prefers to watch quietly and take notes. Her fellow druids call her a bit studious. She is never alone: her big cat, Buddy, shares the camp and likes to scratch now and then, though she insists he is only a lovable kitty.

title: Quagg Ridge
body: Quagg Ridge, east of the Cenarion Watchpost, is the land of the bog lords and fungal giants, towering creatures of living fungus. Many of them are starving. Lately they have been crossing the road to the Spawning Glen to devour the sporelings' spore sacs, and husked mushroom remains lie discarded across the ridge. The sporelings have always kept the bog lords at bay with spears and stones, but the giants have grown more aggressive, or more desperate, and no longer fear them.

title: The Spawning Glen
body: The Spawning Glen, west of the Cenarion Watchpost, is where young sporelings come from. Their spore sacs grow here, starting large and shrinking as the air inside them is spent, until only small, mature sacs remain. It is a fragile nursery, and it is under attack: starving fungal giants and bog lords wander through the glen devouring the sacs. The sporeling Fahssn keeps a desperate watch over them and begs any friendly outsider who passes to save as many as can be saved.

title: Sporeggar
body: Sporeggar is the village of the sporelings, a small and mostly peaceful people, on the western side of Zangarmarsh between Sporewind Lake and Marshlight Lake. It is grown from tallstalk mushrooms raised from fertile spores, and much of it has had to be regrown after attacks by the bog lords. Glowcap mushrooms serve the sporelings as coin. Their elder, Msshi'fn, welcomes outsiders who prove themselves, though others, like Gshaff, still cannot decide what to make of them. The village has enemies on every side: the bog lords, the marsh walkers of old, the spore giants of the Underbog and the Bloodscale naga to the northeast.

title: Marshlight Lake and Bloodscale Enclave
body: Marshlight Lake, in the west of the marsh, is the haunt of bogstroks, whose hatchlings swarm the shallows, and of a giant among them called Terrorclaw. On its shore the Bloodscale naga keep the Bloodscale Enclave and the Marshlight steam pump, worked by Wrekt slaves under the whips of slavedrivers and enchantresses. One naga taskmaster is said to amuse himself by sending slaves out to the lake's islands just when Terrorclaw is ready to feed, and the enclave's naga have also been killing the sporelings of nearby Sporeggar.

title: Zabra'jin
body: Zabra'jin is the Darkspear town in the west of the marsh, overseen by Shadow Hunter Denjai, who commands the trolls' forces in Zangarmarsh. Witch Doctor Tor'gash reads omens in burstcap spores and keeps two pet murlocs, Gargle and Gurgle, while Seer Janidi says he need only ask the spirits. Gambarinka has given up rusting metal tools for the blades of marshfang slicers, Zurjaya is glad of fishing water after the wastes of Hellfire, and a captured gnome repairs gear under a guard who threatens to eat him. Yet the town is hemmed in by ogres cutting their way from the north and Daggerfen assassins on the roads, and a messenger from Garadar has come begging for help.

title: Daggerfen Village
body: Daggerfen Village lies in the northwest of the marsh, west of the Orebor Harborage. Its people, the Daggerfen, are the most cunning and aggressive of the marsh's Lost One tribes, a whole tribe of assassins who brew a potent poison from a ragveil base. They make no secret of wanting to rule the other Lost Ones, and under Chieftain Mummaki they have killed many scouts and messengers, Kurenai, draenei and troll alike, in a bid to seize the roads. Not everything here is grim: a few baby murlocs splash among the huts, though the marsh is said to have no murlocs of its own.

parts.body: The murlocs are a gift. Witch Doctor Tor'gash of Zabra'jin, who keeps two pet murlocs of his own, decided the marsh was missing them and had a cage of colorful young murlocs set loose by the village's northeastern huts, and he hopes the little Lost Ones are enjoying them.

title: Hewn Bog
body: The Hewn Bog, in the north of the marsh, has earned its name. Ango'rosh ogres have moved in and are chopping down its giant mushrooms, a cutting operation overseen by the brute Boss Grog'ak, and the felling threatens to cut a path to the walls of Zabra'jin. Ogres and their shamans now swarm where the mushroom forest stood, and the Kurenai of the Orebor Harborage watch them draw ever closer to their temple.

parts.body: The harm reaches farther than it seems. Mushrooms from the bog match the husks found discarded on Quagg Ridge: this is where the bog lords once came to feed. With their food cut down and carried off by the ogres, the starving giants have turned on the sporelings' spawning grounds instead.

title: Ango'rosh Grounds and Stronghold
body: Northwest of Zabra'jin, the Ango'rosh ogres hold lands of their own. The Ango'rosh Grounds are an armed camp of brutes, maulers, warlocks and sentries under Captain Krosh and Captain Bo'kar. Beyond the camp, a fallen mushroom bridges the water to a small floating island, and in a cave there lies the Ango'rosh Stronghold, stacked with boxes of harvested mushrooms and held by maulers, souleaters, shadowmages and Mal'druk the Soulrender. Its master is Overlord Gorefist, the leader who holds the whole tribe together.

parts.body: The camp holds more than tents and weapons. Plans found here show the Ango'rosh making ready to fall on Zabra'jin, proof that their mushroom cutting so close to the troll town was no accident.

title: Orebor Harborage
body: In the ruins of an old draenei temple northwest of Serpent Lake, a small band of Broken has made a home. These are the Kurenai, Broken who wish to reunite with their draenei kin, sent from their city of Telaar in Nagrand under Ikuti to strengthen ties with Telredor and keep the roads between them open. They are wary of strangers, for wariness has kept them alive. Puluu senses that the temple once meant something to him and hopes the draenei can help him remember. Maktu makes armor of fenclaw hide, and a human who likes to be called the specialist studies the poisons of the Lost Ones.

parts.body: Maktu seldom speaks of it, but he was once a slave himself. Puluu, who has watched a naga taskmaster at Marshlight Lake send his slaves out to feed Terrorclaw, is ashamed that the Kurenai are too few to do more for their enslaved brethren, and hopes the draenei will one day help free the marsh of the naga.

title: Serpent Lake and Bloodscale Grounds
body: Serpent Lake spreads across the north of the marsh. On its eastern shore the Bloodscale naga hold the Bloodscale Grounds and the lake's own steam pump, where overseers, wavecallers and elementals drive Wrekt slaves under the command of the sorceress Rajis Fyashe. The deep water belongs to fenclaw thrashers, swarms of mudfin frenzies and Mragesh, an old and cunning hydra that has dogged many an angler and once nearly made a meal of a Kurenai hunter.

parts.body: Serpent Lake lies at the heart of the naga's design. Schematics taken from them show a hidden network of drains and pumps linking the lakes of the region to it, and at its center a giant drain swallows the water, making the lake a sink for all of Zangarmarsh.

title: Coilfang Reservoir
body: Beneath Serpent Lake, reached through the water, lies Coilfang Reservoir, the stronghold of the naga of the marsh. In its great cavern stone archways lead to the slave pens, the Underbog and the steam vaults, where Warlord Kalithresh is said to command, and deeper still to the Serpentshrine Cavern. At the entrance, Watcher Jhang of the Expedition waits with a twisted ankle for word of four companions who went on inside, and Mortog Steamhead, saved by the Expedition from certain death in the mines, trades with the Expedition's friends.

parts.body: The druids Ysiel Windsinger sent to investigate the giant drain in Serpent Lake were expected back soon after, and they never returned. She has asked her most capable allies to look for them here, near the entrance to the reservoir beneath the lake, and to learn what became of them.

title: Twin Spire Ruins
body: The Twin Spire Ruins stand near the middle of the marsh, the remains of a holy draenei site whose single broken tower, despite the name, still rises over an old burial ground. Both the Alliance and the Horde contest the surrounding marsh: each side strives to hold the two towers that watch over this part of Zangarmarsh and to raise its battle standard over the burial ground, and control passes back and forth as the fighting ebbs and flows. Around the ruins, mudfin frenzies thrash in the shallows and sporebats drift among the stones.

title: Ysiel Windsinger
body: Ysiel Windsinger, a night elf druid, leads the Cenarion Expedition from the Cenarion Refuge. The Expedition began as a small venture of the Cenarion Circle, but it has since grown large and largely independent, though she has not forgotten that it cannot exist without the Circle's support. She came to Outland expecting small pockets of life and found a thriving marsh, then watched its waters fall. Her magic can reshape a willing helper into a form suited to scouting the lakes from the air, and she means to learn why they are falling.

parts.body: The first answer came from Umbrafen Lake: a steam pump worked by the naga was helping to drain the lake. Why they would do it, Ysiel could not say, but at last she understood their hostility toward her druids, and she wasted no time in finding out how widespread their work was.

title: Morthis Whisperwing
body: Morthis Whisperwing is a former member of the Druids of the Talon, the old order that taught young druids the mysteries of flight before the druidic orders came together as the Cenarion Circle. The order is no more, but Morthis means to remain one of them to the end of his days, and he has long searched for an apprentice worthy of the secrets of the stormcrow. He is proud and particular, and pollen makes him sneeze, to his great indignity. He envies the freedom of his two birds, Rook and Corvax, and says he will take wing again once one last task is done.

title: Warden Hamoot
body: Warden Hamoot is in charge of the Cenarion Expedition's security. Ysiel brought wardens with her because she expected some opposition in Outland, but no one foresaw the strength and numbers of the naga, whose lethal attacks began the moment the Expedition set foot in the marsh. While the druids study plants and lakes, Hamoot deals with the hostiles. He pays out the Expedition's bounties on the leaders of the Bloodscale and the Darkcrest, pays for proof of victories over the naga, and has set his sights on the marsh beasts of Funggor Cavern. He never liked the naga of Azeroth, likes these even less, and sheds no tears for them.

title: Ikeyen
body: Ikeyen is a Broken who escaped slavery among the Umbrafen Lost Ones and found safety at the Cenarion Refuge. The druids protect him from the naga and the traitor tribes, and in return he teaches them about the plants and animals of the marsh. Old and weakened, he has lived in fear of his former masters, certain that the Umbrafen would cut his throat if he left the Refuge for even a day. After his escape he hid in a cave south of their village, only to find it fought over by marsh beasts and spore men, and he had to flee again, leaving behind the few things he owned.

parts.body: With Kataru and the Umbrafen seers, witchdoctors and oracles slain, Ikeyen says he will finally sleep comfortably at night. Were he not so old and weak, he would have dealt with his enemies himself, and though he has little to give, he insists that such kindness cannot go unpaid.

title: Anchorite Ahuurn
body: Anchorite Ahuurn leads Telredor. Once a cloistered priest of a quiet retreat, he opened its doors when the orcs fell upon his people and turned the shrine into a haven for refugees, and many draenei owe him their lives. He says Telredor has seen more change in twenty years than in the centuries before, and that the Light has brought him friends he could never have met in his cloister. He hopes to make Telredor a safe home for all who stand with the draenei, has reached out to the Kurenai at the Orebor Harborage, and longs to welcome even the Lost Ones of the marsh back among their people.

parts.body: When he sent an envoy disguised as an arakkoa spirit to the Feralfen, they refused him. He grants that they may choose their own path, and that Elder Kuruti was right about the folly of deceiving them, but he is surprised: he believed every draenei, Broken and Lost Ones included, still remembered that they are one people.

title: Ikuti
body: Ikuti leads the Kurenai at the Orebor Harborage, a band of Broken sent from Telaar in Nagrand to strengthen ties with the draenei of Telredor. He greets visitors kindly but admits that wariness has often been all that stood between his people and death, and his trust must be earned. The Kurenai are content to help the Lost Ones who seek them out, yet unlike some draenei they will not go chasing after the rest, though they act quickly against tribes like the Daggerfen. Those who prove themselves to Ikuti are sent on to Telaar with his word, to Nahuud.

title: Shadow Hunter Denjai
body: Shadow Hunter Denjai oversees Zabra'jin and commands the Darkspear forces in Zangarmarsh. He sent a crew east to build Swamprat Post and give the Horde a presence on the eastern border, and he expects regular reports, which some of his trolls find a trial. Denjai has reason to worry. The Ango'rosh ogres are cutting their way toward his walls, and he cannot believe the place they chose is an accident, while Daggerfen assassins pick off his scouts and messengers and threaten to surround the town. He means to send word north to the orcs of Thunderlord Stronghold, asking for any help they can spare.

parts.body: His suspicion proved right. Plans taken from the Ango'rosh Grounds showed the ogres preparing an attack on Zabra'jin. The stench of ogres, Denjai says, always carries a threat, and now that he has proof of their intentions he means to strike before they do.

body: Msshi'fn is the elder of Sporeggar, called the Sporeggar Primus, and it falls to him to see that his people have what they need. He welcomes outsiders who prove their friendship, even though few of their kind ever come to Sporeggar, and he receives with gratitude the rescued spore sacs that carry the next generation of sporelings. Like the rest of his people he deals in glowcap mushrooms, which the sporelings use as coin, and he will teach a trusted friend how to pick them from the ground without ruining them.

title: Fhwoor
body: Fhwoor is a fungal giant who lives among the sporelings of Sporeggar, an odd sight given how much grief the other giants of the marsh cause them. He speaks simply. He likes the little sporelings, he says, because they saved him, and he does not eat them. He hates the naga and would dearly like to smash them, for the naga have been troubling his little friends, and that makes Fhwoor very angry.

parts.body: In the end Fhwoor marched into the naga village by the Marshlight steam pump, lifted the Ark of Ssslith, the Bloodscale's most prized possession, with ease, and carried it back to Sporeggar, laughing at the squishy naga. The sporelings, who saved him from the naga long ago and have had his help ever since, hope the Bloodscale will take the hint and return to their reservoir.

title: Rajis Fyashe
body: Rajis Fyashe is a naga found on the Bloodscale Grounds, on the eastern shore of Serpent Lake. Overseers and wavecallers stand about her, elementals move among them, and Wrekt slaves toil at the lake's great steam pump under their eyes. She fights with frost and water, hurling bolts of ice, ringing her foes in freezing cold, raising spouts of water beneath them and calling elementals up at their feet, and when sorely wounded she flees to her guards for help. Few reach her without first cutting their way through the naga of the grounds.

parts.body: The Cenarion Expedition has declared a bounty on her. She is the leader of the Bloodscale naga, a sorceress last sighted at Serpent Lake, and the Expedition warns that the Bloodscale are extremely dangerous and that their leader is to be approached only with the greatest caution.

title: Balance Must Be Preserved
body: When the Cenarion Expedition came to Zangarmarsh, its druids expected to find small pockets of life in Outland and found a lush, thriving marsh instead. Their measurements soon told a darker story: the water in the lakes and marshes has been falling steadily ever since they began taking readings, and the impact on the plants and creatures of the marsh could be disastrous. Ysiel Windsinger means to find the cause before it is too late, and sends a helper southwest to Umbrafen Lake to search for clues to the water's loss.

parts.body: The answer at Umbrafen Lake was a steam pump on the shore, worked by naga and drawing the water away. Why the naga would do such a thing, Ysiel could not guess, but it explained their open hostility toward the druids. What it did not show was how far their work reached.

quest 9718 description (offered on turning in 9716: how widespread the naga's activity truly is)

parts.body: To learn that, Ysiel reshaped her helper with a stormcrow amulet and sent them winging over every great lake in the marsh. The flight confirmed her fears: the naga have set up pumping stations at all the major lakes of Zangarmarsh, and they must be stopped if the marsh is to have a future.
sources: quest 9718 description and reward text (Stormcrow Amulet, pumping stations at all the major lakes)

parts.body: She then handed over seeds carrying the rage of the earth, to be sown on the controls of the pumps at Umbrafen Lake, Serpent Lake, Marshlight Lake and the Lagoon. Vines as thick as an arm and as strong as iron choked the machines. The marsh was saved for now, Ysiel said, but this would not be the last of the naga.

title: The Drain Beneath Serpent Lake
body: Drain schematics carried by the Bloodscale naga and the overseers of the steam pumps show an underground system of drains and pumps linking the lakes of Zangarmarsh to Serpent Lake in the north. If the plans are right, a giant drain lies at the very center of the lake, hidden beneath its waters. They are worth confirming. Ysiel Windsinger, who leads the Cenarion Expedition's study of the marsh's falling waters from the Cenarion Refuge, will want to hear at once whether the drain is real, and what it could mean.

parts.body: The drain is real. The naga have turned Serpent Lake into a giant water sink for the rest of the marsh, and Ysiel, who cannot guess their purpose, sent a team of druids to investigate it while she turned to other work.

title: The Bog Lords' Hunger
body: At the Cenarion Watchpost, Watcher Leesa'oh means to learn how the sporelings of Sporeggar live alongside the creatures around them. Her way is patient: watch quietly, take notes, and never interfere without understanding, for all things in nature are bound in one web. There is a great deal to do and she must stay at her camp to organize it, so she sends her helpers out into the field, beginning with a survey of the Spawning Glen to the west, where the young sporelings come from.

parts.body: The survey turned up something alarming: the bog lords of Quagg Ridge were crossing the road to eat the sporelings' spore pods. Leesa'oh guessed they must be starving, and though she would not normally get involved, if they kept eating the pods the sporelings would be wiped out. She sent for dietary clues from the ridge.

parts.body: Husked mushroom remains found on the ridge looked oddly familiar, and samples from the Hewn Bog to the north confirmed her hunch: Ango'rosh ogres had moved in and were cutting down the very mushrooms the bog lords fed on. Even so, Leesa'oh would not hear of wiping out the ogres, who had as much right to the marsh as anyone.

title: The Sporelings' Plight
body: At the Spawning Glen, the sporeling Fahssn begs passing strangers for help. Fungal giants are devouring the spore sacs from which young sporelings come. The sacs start out large and shrink as the air inside them is spent, and only the small, mature ones can be saved. The bog lords are worse. The sporelings have always kept them at bay with spears and stones, but lately the giants have grown more aggressive, or more desperate, and no longer fear sporeling weapons. Fahssn would be forever in the debt of anyone who fought them off.

parts.body: Those who saved the sacs carried them north to Sporeggar, to the elder Msshi'fn. Protecting the next generation earned more than thanks: the sporelings, who could repay such kindness only with their hospitality, welcomed their rescuer into their homes and urged them to stay a while and meet the others, who would surely have many questions.

If the sporelings could take that, they reasoned, worse could follow, and perhaps now the naga would go back to their reservoir.

title: Spirits of the Feralfen
body: Anchorite Ahuurn of Telredor wants to know what has become of the old draenei shrines of the marsh. During the orcs' war his people lost contact with the anchorites who kept them, among them the temple of Boha'mu to the southwest, and he has heard that a tribe of Lost Ones has settled there and may even be using the ruins. At Zabra'jin, Seer Janidi has his own interest in the same tribe. The Feralfen are said to be the most powerful Lost Ones in the marsh and to possess potent medicine, and Janidi wants their totems, for anything that might help him channel the spirits of this world cannot be ignored.

parts.body: The Feralfen had made the ruins their own, as if they remembered something of their heritage, and Ahuurn began to hope the temple could be the key to redeeming the Lost Ones. Their idols showed a fixation on birds, though no birds live in the marsh, and he guessed they had met the arakkoa and taken them for bird spirits.

parts.body: So he brewed a potion to lend his envoy the shape of an arakkoa, and in that guise the envoy greeted Elder Kuruti at the temple. The elder saw through it. His people wanted nothing from the draenei who had turned their backs on them, he said, least of all a redemption offered through trickery, and he asked to be left in peace in his temple.

title: The Withering of the Dead Mire
body: At Telredor, Vindicator Idaar has noticed a disturbing change in the land to the northeast: virtually all life there has begun to wither and die, seemingly without explanation, and he wants a sample of its soil to test his ideas. At Swamprat Post the trolls call the same place the Dead Mire. No one has ever reported seeing anything alive there, and Scout Jyoba, who volunteered to explore it, left three days ago and has not returned. Some who fight the withered giants carry away a strange, sickly basidium and wonder what it once did.

parts.body: The soil Idaar studied was nearly devoid of moisture, and if the ground itself is drying, the creatures of the mire must be suffering terribly. The pain drives the withering giants mad. They are beyond saving, Idaar judged, so the kindest course is to end their suffering.

parts.body: Jyoba was found dead beside his spilled inkwell, his weapon still sheathed, taken by surprise as he wrote. His report was recovered from the withered giants that killed him. It said the fungal giants had gone berserk from the lack of moisture, and Zurai ordered his men to keep away: the post can afford no more losses.

quest 9772 description and reward text (withered giants, berserk from lack of moisture, avoid the area)

parts.body: The basidium told more. Ruam at Telredor and Reavij at Swamprat Post each recognized it and knew what it meant: the Dead Mire had once been a lake like the others and the giants' spawning ground, and with the water gone they can no longer spore. If it goes on, the giants may disappear entirely.

title: The Ango'rosh Threat
body: The Ango'rosh ogres are pressing on both sides of the marsh. At Zabra'jin a wanted poster calls for the head of Boss Grog'ak, overseer of the mushroom cutting north of the town, whose brutes are chopping a path toward its walls. At the Orebor Harborage, Ikuti of the Kurenai watches the same ogres strip the Hewn Bog of its towering mushrooms and creep ever closer to the old temple his people shelter in, and he asks any who would call themselves friends to fight them. The heart of the tribe lies in the Ango'rosh Stronghold, a cave on a small island beyond a fallen mushroom.

parts.body: Grog'ak's head troubled Denjai more than it pleased him. The ogres, he said, had been filtering down from the northern mountains for some time, and the position of their cutting could be no accident. Attack plans seized in the ogres' camp to the northwest proved him right: the ogres were preparing to attack Zabra'jin, and the trolls had to act first.

parts.body: Ikuti's call held the ogres back for the moment, but he was sure they would not give up so easily: the stubbornness of ogres is a memory that has outlasted much of his life as a draenei. The centerpiece of any ogre tribe is its leader, he says, and without one the Ango'rosh would fall to fighting over who leads next.

title: The Raven God
body: Before all the druidic orders came together as the Cenarion Circle, the Druids of the Talon taught promising young druids the mysteries of flight. The order is gone, and its former members teach the skill sparingly, but Morthis Whisperwing still searches for a suitable apprentice. Few druids have truly mastered all the forms open to them. Those who show the promise he requires are sent to him at the Cenarion Refuge in Zangarmarsh, to learn, if he finds them worthy, the secrets of the stormcrow.

parts.body: Morthis took the druid as his apprentice, on the condition that they do all he asks. The relics used to teach the ways of the stormcrow were entrusted long ago to an ancient druid, now deep in slumber, who must be woken. For the Ward of Waking, Morthis needs common herbs and the fragile bogblossoms that grow atop the tallest mushrooms of the marsh.

parts.body: The relics came back from Moonglade, and with them word that troubled Morthis: he could recall no mention of outside forces tampering with the Emerald Dream, and a raven had been seen in the barrow den. He knew of a resurgent arakkoa cult in Blade's Edge that venerates a raven god, and sent his apprentice to Arthorn Windsong at the Evergrove to learn whether the two were linked.

parts.body: Arthorn and the scholar Timeon had learned that a book of the raven was the cult's ancient scripture, destroyed by arakkoa priests who held the cultists heretics. Its stone fragments, buried near Skettis, were gathered and pieced together. The Book of the Raven gave the god's name, Anzu, and a prophecy that he would haunt the dreams of his enemies, twisting them to return to this world.
